patch.value: The bounded legacy MCP compatibility set stops one revision short of the spec's own legacy boundary, so every current host is refused at initialize and the dual-era guarantee is unmet

Measured live on 2026-08-30 against the released stdio entrypoint plugins/pm-claude/scripts/pm-mcp-server.mjs.

Claude Code 2.1.251 opens with initialize and protocolVersion 2025-11-25. The server answers JSON-RPC error -32022 'Unsupported legacy MCP protocol version' with data.supported = ['2025-06-18']. The connection never establishes. The same refusal reproduces for 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26 and, remarkably, for 2026-07-28 itself: sending the server its own canonical revision on the only entrypoint a host actually opens is answered by an unsupported-version error naming a revision two generations old.

The modern surface is healthy. A direct server/discover carrying _meta protocolVersion 2026-07-28 returns a full DiscoverResult with supportedVersions ['2026-07-28'], three negotiated extensions and instructions. So the capability exists and is unreachable through the handshake every legacy-era host uses.

The 2026-07-28 specification defines the boundary this set was supposed to track. Its Versioning and Compatibility page states the terminology directly: legacy means the versions that establish a session with an initialize handshake, namely 2025-11-25 and earlier. The compatibility matrix promises that a legacy client against a dual-era server Works, and that the server answers initialize and serves the client according to the negotiated legacy revision. pm declares itself dual-era and ships the adapter that makes that promise, but its accepted legacy set is the single literal ['2025-06-18'] and therefore omits 2025-11-25, the final and current legacy revision named by the specification pm claims conformance to.

The mechanism is a hand-maintained accept list that no gate compares against the specification's own legacy boundary. The string 2025-11-25 does not appear anywhere in src, docs, tests, plugins or packages. The legacy adapter additionally answers with PM_MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS[0] rather than the version the client requested, so even after the set widens a client that negotiates the newer revision would be told the older one.

This is the export-map denominator family again, in the transport layer: the surface the outside world resolves is one set, and the checker consults a shorter hand list that was already stale when it was written.

The accepted legacy revision set covers every initialize-era revision the referenced specification names as legacy, and 2025-11-25 is accepted; A live handshake from the released stdio entrypoint succeeds for each accepted legacy revision, proving the set is exercised end to end rather than asserted in a unit test; The initialize response echoes the revision the client negotiated rather than a fixed element of the accepted set; An unsupported request still fails and names every supported revision, so widening the set cannot be used to accept anything; A gate fails when the accepted set omits a revision the project's own conformance documentation lists as supported, so the set can never silently lag the specification again; A negative control proves the gate fails on the pre-fix accept list

value.text:
Reproduced, fixed, and gated on 2026-08-30.

Reproduction, before the fix, against the released stdio entrypoint plugins/pm-claude/scripts/pm-mcp-server.mjs:
- initialize protocolVersion 2025-11-25 (what Claude Code 2.1.251 sends, captured on the wire through a logging shim) returned -32022 with data.supported ['2025-06-18']; the host reported 'Failed to connect'.
- initialize with 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26 and 2026-07-28 were refused identically, so the server refused its own canonical revision on the entrypoint every legacy-era host opens.
- server/discover carrying _meta protocolVersion 2026-07-28 returned a complete DiscoverResult with supportedVersions ['2026-07-28'] and three negotiated extensions, proving the capability existed and was unreachable through the handshake rather than absent.

Root cause: PM_MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS was the single literal ['2025-06-18']. The canonical revision's Versioning and Compatibility page defines legacy as the initialize-handshake versions, 2025-11-25 and earlier, and its compatibility matrix promises that a legacy client against a dual-era server works and is served according to the negotiated legacy revision. The accept list was a hand-maintained subset of that boundary and nothing compared the two. The adapter also answered PM_MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS[0] rather than the requested revision, so widening the set alone would still have stranded a client on a version it did not negotiate.

Fix: the accept set now carries the full initialize-era boundary newest-first; resolveLegacyProtocolVersion echoes the negotiated revision, offers the newest revision when protocolVersion is omitted, and refuses anything else with -32022 naming every supported revision, because a legacy client has no fall-forward mechanism and that error text is its only diagnostic.

Verification after the fix:
- initialize 2025-11-25 negotiates 2025-11-25; initialize 2025-06-18 negotiates 2025-06-18; initialize 2024-11-05 is refused with supported ['2025-11-25','2025-06-18'].
- claude mcp list now reports pm-mcp Connected, end to end from the same host that failed.
- tests/integration/mcp-handshake.spec.ts 40 passed, tests/integration/mcp-stateless-protocol.spec.ts 12 passed, tests/unit/sdk/mcp/protocol.spec.ts 6 passed, plugin smoke unit specs 30 passed.
- Both real-process smokes print 'protocol handshake matrix: ok (negotiated 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18; unsupported refused)'.

Gate: assertProtocolHandshakeMatrix reads the revision list from the built SDK by dynamic import rather than restating it, so the matrix iterates the artifact the transport actually accepts instead of a second hand list. That is the property the pre-fix code lacked. Negative control run explicitly: declaring an extra revision 2025-03-26 that the transport does not accept makes the matrix fail with 'Unsupported legacy MCP protocol version' rather than passing, so the gate can fail for the reason it exists.

The sdk:surface gate refused the constant change until a breaking-change reason was recorded, which is the surface governance working as designed; the acknowledgement is in sdk/public-surface.json.

value.negative_control: Declaring a revision the transport does not accept (2025-03-26) in the matrix input makes assertProtocolHandshakeMatrix throw "Unsupported legacy MCP protocol version" instead of passing, so the gate can fail for the reason it exists.

patch.value: Every initialize-era revision the canonical specification names as legacy completes a handshake against the released stdio entrypoint, and the negotiated revision is the one the client requested.

2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 both negotiate and echo the requested revision; 2024-11-05 and 2025-03-26 are refused with -32022 naming both supported revisions; Claude Code 2.1.251 reports pm-mcp Connected where it previously reported Failed to connect.

Widened the initialize-era accept set to the specification's own legacy boundary, made the handshake echo the negotiated revision, and gated the pairing with a real-process matrix read from the built SDK plus a proven negative control. Verified end to end: the host that could not connect now connects.

value.text:
Hosted CI follow-up for a326ad61f, resolved in the next commit.

Two gates failed hosted that the local pass had not exercised. Gates (static) failed on ESLint, which pnpm quality:static does not run locally: assertProtocolHandshakeMatrix scored complexity 20 against a maximum of 16, and a let initialiser was flagged as a useless assignment. Gates (coverage) failed because the new matrix code sat at 58 percent line coverage inside a file whose exports had only spawn-plumbing tests.

Both are now fixed rather than waived. The matrix is decomposed into negotiateLegacyRevision, assertUndeclaredRevisionRefused and assertModernRevisionDiscoverable, which drops it under the complexity ceiling and makes each property independently testable. Nine tests were added over the mocked child: the full declared-set walk, the SDK-derived fallback when no list is supplied, the empty-list refusal, an answered revision the client did not request, a handshake without server identity, an accepted undeclared revision, a non-protocol rejection that must rethrow, discovery omitting the canonical revision, and discovery returning no result. One genuinely dead branch was removed rather than covered: the harness rejects only with Error instances, so the non-Error arm of the refusal message was unreachable.

Local verification after the fix: coverage 100/100/100/100 with zero uncovered counts, eslint . --max-warnings=0 clean, pnpm quality:static exit 0, both real-process smokes print the matrix line, and the declared-but-unaccepted-revision negative control still fails for the right reason.

Worth recording as a method note: the local preflight named by the contributing docs does not include the lint step that hosted CI runs, so a change can pass every local gate and fail Gates (static) on lint alone. That is a smaller instance of the local-versus-hosted divergence tracked on pm-4o7tlx.
